question: Atrophic non-union always requires both bone grafting and stable internal fixation because it lacks biological healing potential.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. Atrophic non-union has absent callus and poor vascularity; unlike hypertrophic non-union (which needs only stability), atrophic type requires both graft and fixation.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Atrophic non-union lacks the cellular and vascular environment for healing; bone graft (autograft preferred) restores biological potential, and rigid fixation provides mechanical stability — both are required.
